question: Should OpenClaw expose acknowledgement, supersession, and decision-marking of durable wake obligations as permanent public operator.write Gateway and CLI controls?
rationale: The implementation can provide these controls, but new protocol, operator-write, persisted-state, and recovery behavior is a compatibility-sensitive product boundary; tests cannot determine whether it should be a supported public contract or a narrower internal recovery surface.

options.title: Approve bounded public controls
options.body: Keep the read and write surfaces, but require complete RPC documentation, exact transition rules, upgrade proof, and live persisted-state evidence before merge.

options.title: Ship inspection first
options.body: Retain read-only list and inspect methods now, and defer state-changing controls until their operator workflow and compatibility contract are separately approved.

options.title: Keep controls internal
options.body: Remove public Gateway and CLI mutations and expose them only through a maintainer-owned doctor or recovery workflow.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded public controls
recommendation.body: Keep the read and write surfaces, but require complete RPC documentation, exact transition rules, upgrade proof, and live persisted-state evidence before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice affects permanent core Gateway, CLI, persisted-state, and recovery contracts rather than a narrow implementation detail.
